prerequisites: Elasticity and Strength of Materials I and II

learning_outcomes.text: That students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their field of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific or ethical issues.
That students have developed the learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competences that are usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their area of study.
That students can transmit information, ideas, problems and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.
Knowledge and capacities for the calculation and design of structures and industrial constructions.
Knowledge and capacities for the application of materials engineering.
Ability to work, lead and manage conflicts in a multidisciplinary group and/or a multilingual environment.
Ability to apply new technologies including information and communication technologies.
Ability for information management, handling and application of technical specifications and necessary legislation for engineering practice.
Respect for human rights and for those with disabilities and willingness to eliminate discriminatory factors based on gender, origin, etc.

syllabus_topics: PROFESSIONAL ATTRIBUTIONS OF THE ENGINEER IN CONSTRUCTION.
BLOCK A: SOIL MECHANICS AND FOUNDATIONS.
TOPIC 1: THE FIELD OF SOIL MECHANICS.
TOPIC 3: IDENTIFICATION OF GRANULAR AND FINE SOILS.
TOPIC 4: NATURAL STRESSES IN THE GROUND.
TOPIC 6: EARTH PRESSURE AND RETAINING STRUCTURES.
BLOCK B: CONSTRUCTION SYSTEMS IN BUILDING.
TOPIC 13: ENCLOSURES AND PAVEMENTS IN BUILDINGS.
TOPIC 17: WATER SUPPLY AND SANITATION NETWORKS.
TOPIC 18: ELECTRICAL ENERGY AND TELEPHONY NETWORKS.
teaching_methods: Explanation of theory and general examples
Field visits to industries, installations and construction sites

assessment_methods.method: Attendance and/or participation in in-person and/or virtual activities
Theoretical concepts of the subject (Theoretical exam)
Completion of assignments, cases or exercises (1 Individual Assignment + 1 Group Assignment)
Laboratory/field practices/use of ICT tools (Site visit with report delivery)

assessment_rules: The grading system will be governed by RD 1125/2003 of September 5, which establishes the European credit system and the grading system in official university degrees. It will be necessary to score above zero in both theoretical and operative content of the subject. The weight of theoretical content in the exam will be 30% versus 70% for operative content (problems). To pass the subject, it is mandatory to independently pass the Theoretical Exam, the course assignments, and attend the scheduled site visit(s).
